newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent steadies, other North Sea crudes sink.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent steadies, other North Sea crudes sink.

text.p: Dated Brent steadied on Tuesday as an end February overhang began to clear, but most other North Sea crudes were set for further losses with March sales still slow, traders said.
A Feb 26-28 Brent traded at Mar Brent -25 cents early in the day to a refiner, two cents firmer than a deal for the same dates on Monday, but another end month cargo was still on offer.

Details also emerged of a March 3-5 deal on Monday at Mar Brent -15 cents. Traders said Brent could attract U.S. interest if the April Brent-WTI spread holds above $1.50 a barrel. It was pegged at $1.64 at midday on Tuesday.

Brent CFDs reflected the firmer tone, with next week's dates (Feb 24-28) bid a couple of cents firmer at April Brent +13 cents. The Feb 18-21/Feb 24-28 contango almost disappeared with the roll talked either side of evens.
In contrast to Brent and Forties, which saw active trade late last week clearing out most March 1-15 supply at around Dated +40/+45 cents, other grades were starting to slide.
Statoil's reduction of Statfjord B and C output on Tuesday by a combined 63,000 barrels per day (bpd) as bad weather continued to prevent offshore loadings failed to support the grade, traders said.
A Statfjord loading Mar 6-8 fetched Dated Brent +36 cents, four cents cheaper than a deal on Monday.
Oseberg was also under pressure, a distressed February cargo trading in the low +20s on Monday and early March barrels were talked around Dated Brent +25/+30 cents.

In the Mediterranean, Urals was unchanged at Dated -90/-80 cents a barrel cif Genoa. Activity was expected to pick up with the reopening of the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk after weather-related closures which lasted much of the past week.
